text:
nina: FYI - pushing kernel v3.9.0 + quant-profile v4.1 to staging @ 21:30 PT. This build includes the async kv alignment patch and a small allocator tweak to reduce ephemeral fragmentation. Anyone object?

cale: No objections. Can we gate on the allocator leak check? Last time we saw fragmentation creep on long sessions.

dez: Add me for the perf watch. I'll run a longer smoke (12m session) against seq_len=4096 scenarios.

ops-bot: Note: create image tag redwood/runtime:staging-2026-04-05-k3.9-q4.1 and pin immutable. CI job 8092 scheduled for preflight.

deploy-bot: preflight started (job: 8092) - tasks: lint, container-scan, kernel-abi-sanity, quant-regression, allocator-smoke. Reports: https://ci.internal/reports/8092

nina: Rollout plan: 21:30 -> 3% canary for 8m, if clean -> 10% for 15m, then evaluate. Rollback window ends 22:10. Emergency pin: `infra tag pin runtime=redwood/runtime:v3.8.9-20260331`

qa-bot: Quick check: quant-regression shows one test flagged: long-seq fp16 drift in beam-search path. Severity: minor. Full output: https://ci.internal/reports/8092#quant-regression

cale: If fp16 drift is only in beam path and not sampling, acceptable if perf is better for token throughput. But let's require p95 <= baseline+100ms and no fragmentation alarms.

[deploy-bot update] preflight finished - allocator-smoke: PASS, kernel-abi-sanity: OK, quant-regression: WARNING (fp16 long-seq drift), container-scan: OK

nina: Starting 3% canary now. Will post back at 21:39 with smoke results.

[~9 minutes later]

nina: Canary 3% done. Quick metrics: error-rate delta +0.2%, p95 +55ms, GPU mem fragmentation events: 2 hosts reported transient bumps but no OOMs. Deployed tag: redwood/runtime:staging-2026-04-05-k3.9-q4.1

dez: My long-smoke ran concurrently. Observed steady throughput improvement ~6% on batch workloads, but the same 2 hosts had fragmentation correlated with a background job. We should re-run after clearing background.

cale: Agree. Hold the 10% ramp until we repro the fragmentation locally. nina - please pause ramp.

nina: Pausing ramp. Initiating targeted repro on the two affected hosts and disabling background maintenance on them. If fragmentation persists, we'll rollback to v3.8.9.

ops-bot: Disabled scheduled maintenance on hosts gpu-34 and gpu-35.

[~7 minutes later]

dez: Repro run complete. Fragmentation did not reoccur once maintenance was off. Looks like a coincident job. Recommending continue to 10%.

cale: +1 continue but add a rolling 5-minute watch after ramp to monitor fragmentation metrics.

nina: OK resuming ramp to 10% now. Deploy will be gradual over 3 waves.

deploy-bot: ramp to 10% started. Monitoring hooks: kv-hitrate, p95, fragmentation-events, allocator-allocs.

[~16 minutes later]

nina: 10% steady for 15m. All checks green. token-level perf: throughput +5.8%, p95 +48ms, fragmentation alerts cleared. Tag ready for canary promotion.

cale: Let's draft release note blurb: "kernel v3.9.0: async KV alignment + allocator tweak; quant-profile v4.1: improved batch throughput with fallbacks for fp16 beam path." I'll drop in docs and request review.

qa-bot: Recommend CI add a small synthetic beam search eval to catch fp16 drift in future CI cycles. Filing issue: https://issues.internal/ENG-4129

nina: Good catch. We'll merge that CI eval after this release. Final step: if everything stays green, we aim to promote to prod during the midnight quiet window. Otherwise rollback to v3.8.9 using the infra pin command above.

deploy-bot: canary cycle complete. All monitoring green.

nina: Thanks everyone. I'll update the release notes and schedule the prod promotion ticket. If you see anything odd ping `runtime-oncall`. :rocket:
